title: Spatchcock Lemon Roast Chicken
seoTitle: Spatchcock Lemon Roast Chicken | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Whole birds flattened with lemon-garlic butter for ten
subtitle: Whole birds flattened with lemon-garlic butter for ten
description: Whole chickens are spatchcocked, seasoned under the skin with lemon-garlic butter, and roasted on sheet pans until golden. Carve into quarters and eighths for fast hall service.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Spatchcock Lemon Roast Chicken in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Spatchcock the birds
steps.instruction: Remove backbones with shears, flatten chickens breast-side up, and tuck wing tips under. Pat completely dry inside and out. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season under the skin
steps.instruction: Mix butter with lemon zest, juice, garlic, and thyme. Loosen breast skin and spread half the butter mix under skin on each bird. Season outside with salt, pepper, and olive oil.

steps.title: Roast on vegetables
steps.instruction: Scatter onion and carrots on two sheet pans. Place spatchcocked birds on top and roast at 425°F until thickest breast hits 165°F and skin is golden, about 50–60 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Rest before carving
steps.instruction: Tent birds with foil and rest 15 minutes so juices settle. Save pan juices and roasted vegetables for service. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Spatchcock Lemon Roast Chicken onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Carve for the line
steps.instruction: Carve each bird into ten portions: legs, thighs, and breast pieces. Arrange on hotel pans with pan juices spooned over. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Insert probe in the thickest part of the breast, not touching bone, for accurate reads.
If skin browns too fast, tent loosely with foil and keep roasting to 165°F internal.
Roasted pan vegetables make an easy side without another pot to wash.
tonightSpread: Carved chicken on platters with pan juices and roasted carrots and onions.
Mashed potatoes or crusty bread to soak up lemon-garlic butter.
leftovers: Strip bones for chicken soup with the roasted vegetable base.
Slice cold breast for sandwiches with mayo and crisp lettuce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Spatchcocking cuts roast time nearly in half and gives every piece crisp skin. Whole bird night feels special without the stress of grilling twenty individual pieces.
mealPrepNotes: Spatchcock birds the morning of and keep on sheet pans in the fridge. Soften butter mix ahead. Rest birds 15 minutes before carving or juices run everywhere.
